--- CHUNK 1 ---
Petition to the Noble, Highly Esteemed Gentlemen Directors. To the illustrious Assembly of the Seventeen Commissioned, Representing the General United Netherlands Chartered East India Company at the Presidential Chamber. In Amsterdam. Noble, Highly Esteemed, Wise, Prudent, and Most Generous Gentlemen.

In dutiful obedience to your Noble Highly Esteemed honored commands contained in their general and secret missive dated the 23rd of September and 13th of December of the past year, directed to the Noble high Government of these Lands, and presented by our President in the Council of Justice, we have the honor to inform your Noble Highly Esteemed by means of these our humble letters, that after an Extract from the Minutes of what was discussed and resolved in the Council of India on the 3rd of July of this year had been brought before the ordinary assembly, whereby information or clarification was requested as to which Members had conducted themselves in a partisan manner on behalf of the former Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier [Adriaan Valckenier:], and specifically in the granting and provision of the unprecedented political Recollections [Recollementen: a form of petition or memorial], both against the Members of the Noble High Government of these Lands, as well as at the expense of all and each individual, and on that same day in fulfillment of that resolution, and for the clarification of their high Excellencies, it was deemed good to present authenticated copies of the opinions concerning the requests made by the aforementioned former Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier regarding the Recollections, which were then resting in the secret files, to their high Excellencies, and further, when our President brought before this Council on the 11th of that same month a further resolution taken on the 5th previously, whereby it became clear to us how their high Excellencies, in accordance with the directive of your Noble Highly Esteemed, had been pleased to order that the Members Mr. Bernhard Jacob Della Faille, Mr. Pieter

--- CHUNK 2 ---
the Recollections, which were then resting in the secret files, to their high Excellencies, and further, when our President brought before this Council on the 11th of that same month a further resolution taken on the 5th previously, whereby it became clear to us how their high Excellencies, in accordance with the directive of your Noble Highly Esteemed, had been pleased to order that the Members Mr. Bernhard Jacob Della Faille, Mr. Pieter Willem Lammens, Mr. Theodorus Polycarpus Woijt, and Mr. Jan Blocquau should abstain from all legal proceedings and judicial authority in the matter of the former Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, and that in their place there had been newly assumed the General Bookkeeper Evert Christoffel Lamus, the Military Captain Rudolph Carel Von Glan, and the Merchants Jan Cornelis Du Quesne and Corijn Stevens, the last-named of whom on that same day and by order of our President came before us and appeared in Council, and took the Oath for the office of Councilor of Justice in the hands of our President, and this oath was likewise at that time renewed and refreshed by his Excellency and the other Members of this Council, in accordance with what was ordained by your Noble Highly Esteemed in the aforementioned secret missive, whereupon, after resumption of the secret directive of your Noble Highly Esteemed mentioned above, the advocate fiscal Mr. Cornelis Phillips was provisionally suspended by this Council, and meanwhile the water fiscal Mr. Jan Hendrik van Panhuijs was ordered to attend to all daily occurring matters concerning the office of advocate fiscal for as long as another should be elected in place of the aforementioned Mr. Cornelis Phillips pro interim, and further, on the recommendation of their high Excellencies in order to proceed with what was demanded by your Noble Highly Esteemed by

--- CHUNK 3 ---
mentioned, the advocate fiscal Mr. Cornelis Phillips was provisionally suspended by this Council, and meanwhile the water fiscal Mr. Jan Hendrik van Panhuijs was ordered to attend to all daily occurring matters concerning the office of advocate fiscal for as long as another should be elected in place of the aforementioned Mr. Cornelis Phillips pro interim, and further, on the recommendation of their high Excellencies in order to proceed with what was demanded by your Noble Highly Esteemed by missives of the 23rd of September, likewise 13th of October, and 13th of December of the past year, in execution of those honored commands, our President asked the other permanent Members of this Council whether one of their Excellencies would be willing to take upon himself the office of Advocate Fiscal provisionally in service of Justice, and after this was declared by the four presiding Members Mr. Jacob Van Den Bosch, Mr. Theodorus Van Reverhorst, Mr. Reijnier Stapel, and Mr. Jacob Pompe van Meerdervoort to be not inclined to do so, our fellow Member Mr. Philippus Rochus Kien requested some days' delay in order to declare himself finally on this matter, which his Excellency having been granted, the President asked the Members of this Council thereupon, so that if his Excellency Kien should not be able to accept the office of advocate fiscal, they would meanwhile let their thoughts turn to a capable and skilled person who in these circumstances of times and matters could and might be entrusted with the aforementioned office provisionally with peace of mind, but with respect to the bailiff Pieter Bookestijn, who according to the ordinance of your Noble Highly Esteemed, just as well as the Advocate Fiscal Mr. Cornelis Phillips, had to be provisionally suspended from his office by this Council, we could not execute the honored order of your Noble Highly Esteemed in this regard,

--- CHUNK 4 ---
a capable and skilled person who in these circumstances of times and matters could and might be entrusted with the aforementioned office provisionally with peace of mind, but with respect to the bailiff Pieter Bookestijn, who according to the ordinance of your Noble Highly Esteemed, just as well as the Advocate Fiscal Mr. Cornelis Phillips, had to be provisionally suspended from his office by this Council, we could not execute the honored order of your Noble Highly Esteemed in this regard, since the same had died some time previously, and another had already been appointed in his place; whereupon subsequently at our assembly on the 18th of July of this year, when the aforementioned Mr. Philippus Rochus Kien declared, after having duly considered the matter, that he wished to refrain entirely from the fiscal office, our President asked the Members whether their Excellencies, in accordance with what had already been noted in the minutes, had let their thoughts turn to a capable and skilled person to whom one could entrust the aforementioned office pro interim with peace of mind, and after this had been taken into consideration, Mr. Nicolaas Iongsma, who was not only experienced in law and had been promoted, but had also practiced for some time in Friesland and here, and had moreover taken on the office of secretary of the magistrates of this city, was thereupon understood to be the only one who possessed the required capability, and was appointed as pro interim advocate fiscal, who then also on that appointment the next day, or indeed on the 19th of July of this year, took the Oath for that office in the hands of our President. And further, on the 23rd of July of this year, it was carefully considered by us how and in what manner one could best and most fittingly accomplish the

--- CHUNK 5 ---
Mr. Nicolaas Iongsma, as the only one who possessed the required capability, and was appointed as pro interim advocate fiscal, who then also on that appointment the next day, or indeed on the 19th of July of this year, took the Oath for that office in the hands of our President. And further, on the 23rd of July of this year, it was carefully considered by us how and in what manner one could best and most fittingly accomplish the demanded inquiry according to the desire and intention of your Noble Highly Esteemed, and thereupon after mature deliberation it was deemed best to issue as soon as possible to the appointed pro interim Advocate Fiscal of India Mr. Nicolaas Iongsma authenticated copies of such three Extracts from the honored directive of your Noble Highly Esteemed as were brought before this Council by our President on the 11th of July previously, to the end that his Excellency might make such use thereof and employ such means in the work as he should deem necessary and fitting in his office and duty for the obtaining of the necessary information and inquiry for the right of the high authority and the true interest of the Company, and in order that all of these should be conducted before Commissioners and the sworn adjunct clerk Pieter Haksteen, to the end that subsequently the Council should receive a written Report of their handling from time to time, and subsequently on the 1st of August of this year, by the pro interim advocate fiscal a Request was presented to this Council with the request that there might be granted to him inventorization and sequestration, or alternatively, in case of unexpected denial of the same, arrest and interdiction upon and against the delivery of all such goods, effects, and cash as there were both on an indirect as well as direct

--- CHUNK 1 ---
Council regarding its handling by means of a written Report to be submitted each time. Subsequently, on the 1st of August of this year, by the then interim advocate fiscal presented to this Council a Request with the petition that there might be granted to him inventorization and sequestration, or alternatively by unexpected revocation of the same arrest and interdiction upon and against the delivery of all such goods, effects, and monies, as there might be, whether in an indirect as well as direct manner, under the Lord Extraordinary Councillor of India Nicolaas Crul [Nicholas Crul], as well as Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, and Johannes van der Linde, as authorized representatives of the former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier [Adrian Valckenier], or anyone else remaining or otherwise to be found here at this place, with an ordinance to all and each of the same to declare to the bailiff or Executor by provisional means under presentation of Oath, and specifically to set forth what and which effects and monies under one or another person, the aforementioned Noble Lord and gentlemen with power of attorney might in any way be known, directly or indirectly remaining, and all of this with such severe Penalties as we after the importance of the matter would understand to be fitting, and that furthermore the granted measure would stand for so long, until there would be further disposed of by this Council, or over the matter in principal upon the arrival of the aforementioned Lord Valckenier, so on that same day to the Pro interim Advocate fiscal by Provisional means there was granted by us arrest and interdiction upon and against the delivery of all such goods, effects, and monies, as there might be, whether in a direct as well as indirect manner under the aforementioned Noble Lord Crul, as well as the gentlemen Helvetius and van der Linden as authorized representatives of the aforementioned former Governor-General Valckenier or anyone else remaining, or here at

--- CHUNK 2 ---
be disposed of, so on that same day by us to the Pro interim Advocate fiscal by Provisional means there was granted arrest and interdiction upon and against the delivery of all such goods, effects, and monies, as there might be, whether in a direct as well as indirect manner under the aforementioned Noble Lord Crul, as well as the gentlemen Helvetius and van der Linden as authorized representatives of the aforementioned former Governor-General Valckenier or anyone else remaining, or here at this place to be found, and we further understand that the same arrest and interdiction would stand for so long, until by this Council further or over the matter in principal upon the arrival of the aforementioned Lord Valckenier would be disposed of, and the same gentlemen with power of attorney were ordered to give most speedily to the bailiff of this Council a proper specification of all such goods and monies, etc., as might have remained under their Excellencies and further persons, and up to now are remaining, but the further petition made by the aforementioned Request was, for the time being, denied, when by our bailiff the aforementioned disposition was first executed, so the aforementioned gentlemen with power of attorney upon the made insinuation to the said bailiff delivered such documents and papers as by the execution that was hereto attached became known, can be further examined as it pleases. — And the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate fiscal further on the 12th of September of this year made known to this Council, that upon the raised difficulty of the secretary of this Council his Excellency requested, that as well as his Predecessors might enjoy such a resolution as by the Council on the date of 12th January 1735 had been taken, and therefore in copy to be able to obtain such Minutes as by their High Excellencies, the Noble high Government of these Lands, and the resolutions of

--- CHUNK 3 ---
Advocate fiscal on the 12th of September of this year made known to this Council, that upon the raised difficulty of the secretary of this Council his Excellency requested, that as well as his Predecessors might enjoy such a resolution as by the Council on the date of 12th January 1735 had been taken, and therefore in copy to be able to obtain such Minutes as by their High Excellencies, the Noble high Government of these Lands, and the resolutions of this Council following thereupon of the dates 3rd, 11th, 18th July, as his Excellency declared to be necessary in his office; when by the Council by plurality of votes it was understood that the aforementioned Copy was to be included under the aforementioned resolution, after which the said pro interim advocate fiscal, on the 19th following thereupon again addressed himself with a petition to this Council, and thereby made known that his Excellency, in accordance with the aforementioned resolution of the Council in copy, had indeed obtained the aforementioned required Minutes, without that his Excellency on account of the difficulty made by the secretary had yet been able to obtain the copy of certain advices concerning the granting of unheard and political recollections for the benefit of the former Lord Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier, which his Excellency declared as serving most to his purpose, and as the Corpus delicti [body of the crime] was necessary to have, for which reason his Excellency was petitioning this Council, that the secretary might be elucidated thereupon, and if necessary ordered to deliver the aforementioned copy of the same advices to his Excellency at the very earliest, which petition by this Council was likewise granted and considered by majority of votes, as an appendix and sequel to that which had been granted to his Excellency by minute of the 12th of September of this year aforementioned here; And we have

--- CHUNK 4 ---
Excellency was petitioning this Council, that the secretary might be elucidated thereupon, and if necessary ordered to deliver the aforementioned copy of the same advices to his Excellency at the very earliest, which petition by this Council was likewise granted and considered by majority of votes, as an appendix and sequel to that which had been granted to his Excellency by minute of the 12th of September of this year aforementioned here; And we have further upon received order from their High Excellencies by Minute of the date 20th of the same aforementioned month of September in the presence of Commissioners from our Council caused to be published a notice, whereby their High Excellencies in accordance with the letter from your Noble High Esteemed by their esteemed missive of the 13th of December of the past year promised to everyone an act of impunity to the giver of the money, or money's value, if he might come to discover the taker, such that thereof it would be convinced that one would then in such a case, by all possible means help the giver, to obtain from the taker restitution of his disbursed money, or money's value, but although this has been done with good intention, the same has been of little fruit up to now, so that your Noble High Esteemed will be able to see from the written reports by commissioners for inquiry delivered to this Council, as evidence how the old governor of Java's North East Coast Bartholomeus Visscher [Bartholomew Visscher], who together with several other persons regarding the buying and selling of offices was heard on interrogatories, maintained that upon certain questions put to him he was not obliged to answer, which the said Commissioners ad Referendum [for referral] having held to this Council, we have judged ourselves to be incompetent to employ any coercive measures against the aforementioned persons, and accordingly understand the aforementioned Visscher with his given responses

--- CHUNK 5 ---
evidence how the old governor of Java's North East Coast Bartholomeus Visscher [Bartholomew Visscher], who together with several other persons regarding the buying and selling of offices was heard on interrogatories, maintained that upon certain questions put to him he was not obliged to answer, which the said Commissioners ad Referendum [for referral] having held to this Council, we have judged ourselves to be incompetent to employ any coercive measures against the aforementioned persons, and accordingly understand the aforementioned Visscher with his given responses to be sufficient, and further deemed it good that Commissioners for inquiry should proceed on the footing begun by them, whereupon the said officer having raised his objection and requested that we would intercede with their High Excellencies for another act of impunity, whereby a penalty would be established, so the same petition was understood by us to be held in status until regarding the buying and selling of offices more persons would have been heard. That further on the 24th of November thereafter by Commissioners for inquiry again delivered a written Report, and thereby made known that the secretary of the gentlemen aldermen of this city Anthonij Isaac Cassa, the Procurator Mr. Willem Cras, together with the sworn Clerk of the Council Paul Fredrik Eversoon, who regarding the drawing up and bringing of the declarations and recollections at the house of Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius were questioned, had likewise maintained that they were not obliged to answer specifically, so that by the Report of the said Commissioners (if it please) they may be seen; but the aforementioned evasions as merely practiced, to be if possible the truth of the matter withheld from us, rejected, and they are condemned on such articles as were respectively put to them, and by them were refused to answer specifically according to truth, and which last case we here deemed best to

--- CHUNK 1 ---
sustained without being held, to answer specifically, to be included in the Report of the aforementioned Commissioners (if it pleases); but the aforementioned evasions, as they were merely practiced, in order, if it were possible, to withhold the truth of the matter from us, were rejected, and they were condemned on such articles as were respectively presented to them, and which they had refused to answer specifically according to truth, and which last case we here, for the best connection of matters, have deemed necessary to allow to follow, and all the obtained depositions together with the Reports received concerning this, which up to this date in this troublesome matter have been legally filed, we send herewith for the consideration of your Noble High Excellency, and shall further proceed to inform your Noble High Excellency that the assumed Member, the chief merchant, and elected head administrator Corijn Stevens, by virtue of his impending departure to Cochim [Kochi], has been discharged from the Council, and in his place has again been assumed the old Persian governor Carel Coenat, who on the 3rd of October thereafter, after taking the customary Oath, was introduced, as when on the aforementioned day by the Pro interim Advocate Fiscal of India Mr. Nicolaas Jongsma a Request was delivered to this Council, and thereupon submitted an interrogatory on the first and second previously answered before Commissioners by the Merchant Henry Abbis cum suis [and his associates], and likewise at the end of the same requested that on the persons of Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, ordinary Member in the Council, and Mr. Cornelis Phillips, suspended Advocate Fiscal of India might be granted corporal apprehension and incarceration at least upon unexpected withdrawal of that pledge, and this on the ground that the same would have made themselves guilty of an unlawful and inhuman massacre of a multitude of Chinese, the first in the hospital of that nation, and the last

--- CHUNK 2 ---
end of the same requested that on the persons of Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, ordinary Member in the Council, and Mr. Cornelis Phillips, suspended Advocate Fiscal of India might be granted corporal apprehension and incarceration at least upon unexpected withdrawal of that pledge, and this on the ground that the same would have made themselves guilty of an unlawful and inhuman massacre of a multitude of Chinese, the first in the hospital of that nation, and the last-named in the Company's [VOC's] stocks, is by this Council upon the aforementioned request understood to accord the requested pledge provisionally on the persons of the aforementioned Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius and Mr. Cornelis Phillips, and this in their houses, each under the supervision of a bailiff and clerk of the secretariat of this Council, with order to the aforementioned persons to hold such pledge there as long as until further disposition, but without access of any kind except of blood relatives, and further on the same day by this Council deemed good to request of the Noble high Government of these Lands that in the service of Justice, whether by assistance of militia or indeed the placement of the aforementioned Helvetius and Phillips at the gates of this city, the necessary orders be pleased to be given, or otherwise to arrange such other means as according to their customary wisdom would be understood to be proper, whereupon by their High Excellencies it was understood that for the respective dwellings of the pledged persons a sentry would be placed to observe their persons, the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate Fiscal having on the same day, and after the Council's disposition regarding the pledge on the persons of Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius and Mr. Cornelis Phillips had been communicated to him, requested to this Council the inventorying and sequestration of their goods, in particular the seizure of papers or otherwise upon unexpected

--- CHUNK 3 ---
been understood that for the respective dwellings of the pledged persons a sentry would be placed to observe their persons, the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate Fiscal having on the same day, and after the Council's disposition regarding the pledge on the persons of Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius and Mr. Cornelis Phillips had been communicated to him, requested to this Council the inventorying and sequestration of their goods, in particular the seizure of papers or otherwise upon unexpected withdrawal of that interdiction so that none of the same goods or papers be alienated or removed, with such penalties as this Council would understand to be proper, upon which request then also being disposed of, it was understood to accord the last part of the same, and thus the aforementioned Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius and Mr. Cornelis Phillips were interdicted from alienating any of their goods or papers with such penalty as this Council would understand to be proper; and further shortly after this date, upon the complaint brought by the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate Fiscal regarding the access granted to the blood relatives of the pledged persons Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius and Mr. Cornelis Phillips, concerning which matter was dealt with, beyond the measures taken, by this Council it was arrested that they, the pledged persons, must declare which blood relatives they were inclined to speak with, and so that thereafter by the Council such disposition be made regarding this as we would understand to be proper, whereupon by the pledged persons respectively having been made a declaration of their blood relatives and necessary household servants, and after the Pro interim Advocate Fiscal had declared himself regarding this, it was deemed good to accord their requests concerning this, and even to permit to the pledged Mr. Cornelis Phillips moreover that the widow De Roode might come to his wife: when further on the aforementioned 3rd

--- CHUNK 4 ---
be disposed of as we would understand to be proper, whereupon by the pledged persons respectively having been made a declaration of their blood relatives and necessary household servants, and after the Pro interim Advocate Fiscal had declared himself regarding this, it was deemed good to accord their requests concerning this, and even to permit to the pledged Mr. Cornelis Phillips moreover that the widow De Roode might come to his wife: when further on the aforementioned 3rd of October by the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate Fiscal to our Council without the least preliminary foreknowledge of President or Council was presented an ample request tending toward a request for citation in person against the ordinary Members of the Council Mr. Bernard Jacob Della Faille, Mr. Pieter Willem Lammen, the extraordinary Member Mr. Theodorus Polycarpus Woijt, and Mr. Jan Blocquan, likewise the water fiscal Mr. Johan Hendrik Van Panhuijs over and concerning their Excellencies against office, oath, and duty, and against the constant manner of proceeding had accorded unheard political recollections for the benefit of the former Governor General Adriaan Valckenier, but before disposing upon that request, it being deemed good, the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate Fiscal by way of further interpretation to be asked what exactly his intention was, and to what end the requests and conclusions against the aforementioned and water fiscal Members of the Council would come to serve, and thereupon having been declared by him to be a suspension, the aforementioned made request was denied for the present. that further on the 6th of October thereafter, on the occasion that the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate Fiscal made known that the adjunct sworn clerk Pieter Haksteen had made difficulty, to authenticate copies of the aforementioned opinions, as copies together with citation, and to grant them to the same, with the request that he might be qualified for this,

--- CHUNK 5 ---
serve, and thereupon having been declared by him to be a suspension, the aforementioned made request was denied for the present. that further on the 6th of October thereafter, on the occasion that the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate Fiscal made known that the adjunct sworn clerk Pieter Haksteen had made difficulty authenticating copies of the aforementioned opinions as copies together with citation and granting them to the same, with the request that he might be qualified for this, it being discovered by the Council that he, the Pro interim Advocate Fiscal, was of the intention to proceed against the aforementioned Members of the Council and water fiscal in the ordinary manner, by this Council it was arrested to interdict him, the Pro interim Advocate Fiscal, from proceeding with the citation in the ordinary manner against the aforementioned Members and water fiscal, and likewise to forbid the adjunct sworn clerk to authenticate and deliver any copies of the aforementioned opinions, and to persist in the decision of the 3rd hereof cited above. After which on the 13th of October thereafter, by the President to the Council was communicated that the aforementioned four Members and water fiscal had addressed themselves to their High Excellencies with a request to be permitted to obtain elucidation, or whether your Noble High Excellency had recommended to their High Excellencies to have them take action, but in case of no, that their Excellencies had then requested that the Pro interim Advocate Fiscal might be interdicted from undertaking any procedures against them, and likewise to give them proper satisfaction regarding their injured honor and propriety, but that the same request had been placed in the hands of the aforementioned Pro interim Advocate Fiscal to make his response against it, shortly thereafter the aforementioned officer to the Council has requested, before being permitted to know whether we would be pleased to involve ourselves regarding this

--- CHUNK 1 ---
had requested that the pro interim advocate fiscal might be interdicted from undertaking any proceedings against them, and likewise that they be given appropriate satisfaction regarding their injured honor and reputation. However, this same request had been placed in the hands of the aforementioned pro interim advocate fiscal, so that he might make his response against it. Shortly thereafter, the aforementioned officer requested of the Council, before being permitted to know whether we would be pleased to involve ourselves with him by supplying our advice for the support and corroboration of his response, because he believed that the same request was purely a matter of justice and belonged to this Council. However, it being understood by majority of votes that his response should be allowed to proceed as would be deemed most advisable, and further that we should address ourselves to their High Excellencies with the request that the aforementioned Request from the said ordinary Members and water fiscal should not be disposed of, but rather that the same, being a matter of justice, should be referred to this Council for decision. Before we could hear any disposition on this matter, their High Excellencies, by resolution dated the 19th, were pleased to demand from this court of justice all such secret and other papers, as well as dispositions and minutes, whether they might contain the delivery of secret advice and other papers, as well as interdictions, or however they might be named, as might be held and have occurred in this Council, regarding the aforementioned request of the pro interim advocate fiscal for the citation in person of the aforementioned said water fiscal, as well as those matters relating to the actions of the aforementioned pro interim advocate fiscal, both before and after the said request, to the fulfillment of which we have made not the least difficulty in laying open our conduct in this matter and in allowing to be delivered everything that had occurred regarding this matter.

--- CHUNK 2 ---
had occurred regarding this matter, regarding the aforementioned request of the pro interim advocate fiscal for the citation in person of the aforementioned said water fiscal, as well as those matters relating to the actions of the aforementioned pro interim advocate fiscal, both before and after the said request, to the fulfillment of which we have made not the least difficulty in laying open our conduct in this matter and in allowing to be delivered everything that had occurred regarding this matter and been committed to paper, with the declaration that no secret papers concerning this matter were held by the Council, and that we knew nothing of any further or other actions of the pro interim advocate fiscal in this matter. During this deliberation, the aforementioned four Members again saw fit to address themselves to their High Excellencies with an ample Request, now being delivered herewith in copy, from whose contents your Noble High Excellency will not without great astonishment be pleased to perceive how those same Members have dared, under various hastily gathered arguments and incorrect insinuations, to present to their High Excellencies various matters and points which, with regard to their Excellencies, would have been undertaken by this assembly. However, the aforementioned points being examined and considered by us, we have not deemed it unfit to place before your Noble High Excellency in brief and simple terms that the pro interim advocate fiscal, as has been set forth above, without the least prior knowledge of the President or Council, addressed himself with a request in order to obtain a copy of the advice given regarding the granting of the requested recollections by the former Lord Governor General Adriaan Valckenier [Adriaan Valckenier:], which same matter had been agreed to by this Council as cited above, because at that time the same had already been delivered to their High Excellencies, and therefore could no longer be regarded as

--- CHUNK 3 ---
be placed before your Noble High Excellency in brief and simple terms that the pro interim advocate fiscal, as has been set forth above, without the least prior knowledge of the President or Council, addressed himself with a request in order to obtain a copy of the advice given regarding the granting of the requested recollections by the former Lord Governor General Adriaan Valckenier, which same matter had been agreed to by this Council as cited above, because at that time the same had already been delivered to their High Excellencies, and therefore could no longer be regarded as a secret of the Council. However, it was by no means permitted to the pro interim advocate fiscal to employ those against the aforementioned Members in particular, as it pleased them to draw from it, but only because the said officer declared that he needed the same in his office, and as has already been said, as an attachment and consequence of the Minutes of the 12th of September. It is true that the aforementioned pro interim advocate fiscal subsequently, without our prior knowledge, came forward with a request to have the said four Members and water fiscal, Mr. Johan Hendrik van Panhuijs [Johan Hendrik van Panhuijs:], summoned in person, and that the same was denied on that day for the time being, for the reason that one could not then know whether your Noble High Excellency might have taken any further disposition regarding them, who had already been entered in the books as partial and suspect judges. And this request we believe was properly brought before this assembly, because it was judged that, in case they were liable in this regard, the same would be a consequence and sequel of the matter of the former Lord Governor General Adriaan Valckenier, which had been demanded of us by your Noble High Excellency with the attachment thereof. However, not as the aforementioned Members incorrectly, in order to make good their position and to add some appearance to it, have represented, that we

--- CHUNK 4 ---
we believe was properly brought before this assembly, because it was judged that, in case they were liable in this regard, the same would be a consequence and sequel of the matter of the former Lord Governor General Adriaan Valckenier, which had been demanded of us by your Noble High Excellency with the attachment thereof. However, not as the aforementioned Members incorrectly, in order to make good their position and to add some appearance to it, have represented, that we were only ordered to judge regarding the matter of the said Lord Valckenier. It is also further the truth, and can be seen from the minutes of the 6th of October, that the President and four of our permanent Members had made difficulty about voting as judges hereon in the principal, if the pro interim advocate fiscal were permitted by majority of votes to proceed in this matter, but by no means that we were obliged to withdraw ourselves from the disposition taken over the previous requests, much less to allow the aforementioned four Members to prescribe to us laws or lessons regarding what should have been done or left undone in this matter. And thus, on such an unfounded and disadvantageous argument, as if we had gone beyond our judicial office, and besides the fact that the aforementioned difficulties raised by our President and the four Members of this Council have not even been accepted as founded, nor been found weighty enough, we wish from this simple recital of matters gladly to leave to the prudent and penetrating judgment of your Noble High Excellency and an equally impartial consideration, whether we in this matter, refraining altogether from involving ourselves in a particular subtle refutation and rebuttal of the pretended reasonings and arguments for the demonstration of a supposed nullity, which would have been committed in this matter, have not proceeded as fitting judges and said Members, which

--- CHUNK 5 ---
have not even been accepted as founded, nor been found weighty enough, we wish from this simple recital of matters gladly to leave to the prudent and penetrating judgment of your Noble High Excellency and an equally impartial consideration, whether we in this matter, refraining altogether from involving ourselves in a particular subtle refutation and rebuttal of the pretended reasonings and arguments for the demonstration of a supposed nullity, which would have been committed in this matter, have not proceeded as fitting judges and said Members, who have made such a fuss and bad interpretation over this matter, have not secured themselves against those persecutions which they so forcefully measure out, that by the pro interim advocate fiscal, both with respect to their honor as well as regarding their persons, would have been inflicted, and we do not doubt that your Noble High Excellency will fully justify our conduct held in this matter, so that we may continue to exercise our judicial office further with peace of mind according to conscience, and without being interrupted by anyone. By the Lord President, on the 13th of October, it was communicated to the Council that on the day before, on behalf of the detained Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius [Willem Vincent Helvetius:], a Request had been presented to their High Excellencies, tending toward the Recusation [recusal:] both of the aforementioned Lord President as well as the pro interim advocate fiscal, not only with regard to the matter of the said Mr. Willem Vincent Helvetius, but also with respect to that of the former Lord Governor General Adriaan Valckenier, we therefore resolved at that time to request of their High Excellencies an authentic copy of the aforementioned Request, in order to proceed regarding it as would be advised in Council.
